nodes.label: Chapter 1 Scope and Application
nodes.rationale: Administrative provisions governing scope, purpose, application, and enforcement of the California Residential Code.

nodes.label: Section 1.1 General
nodes.rationale: Establishes the title, purpose, and scope of the California Residential Code as Part 2.5 of Title 24.

nodes.label: 1.1.3 Scope
nodes.rationale: Code applies to construction of detached one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses not more than three stories above grade plane.

nodes.label: 1.1.3.1 Classification
nodes.rationale: Structures classified by occupancy with reference to Chapter 3 of California Building Code.

nodes.label: 1.1.4 Appendices
nodes.rationale: Appendix provisions do not apply unless specifically adopted by a state or local agency.

nodes.label: 1.1.5 Referenced Codes
nodes.rationale: Adopts referenced standards/publications as standard reference documents.

nodes.label: 1.1.7 Order of Precedence
nodes.rationale: Specific provisions over general; most restrictive prevail; CRC vs CBC selection rules for one/two-family dwellings.

nodes.label: 1.1.8 Local Amendments
nodes.rationale: Authorizes city/county/local more-restrictive amendments based on climatic, topographic, or geological conditions.

nodes.label: 1.1.9 Effective Date
nodes.rationale: Standards effective at the time of permit application apply to plans and construction.

nodes.label: 1.1.11 Format
nodes.rationale: Adopts IRC by reference chapter-by-chapter; reserved chapters not adopted.

nodes.label: Section 1.8 HCD
nodes.rationale: Department of Housing and Community Development authority over housing construction.

nodes.label: 1.8.2 Authority and Abbreviations
nodes.rationale: HCD is authorized to promulgate building standards for several types of building applications.

nodes.label: 1.8.2.1.1 Housing Construction
nodes.rationale: HCD 1 applications: hotels, motels, lodging houses, apartments, dwellings, dormitories, condominiums, employee housing, factory-built housing.

nodes.label: 1.8.2.1.2 Housing Accessibility
nodes.rationale: HCD 1-AC applications for covered multifamily dwellings serving persons with disabilities.

nodes.label: 1.8.2.1.3 Permanent Buildings in Mobilehome Parks
nodes.rationale: HCD 2 applications: permanent buildings constructed within mobilehome and special occupancy parks.

nodes.label: 1.8.3 Local Enforcing Agency
nodes.rationale: Local building department enforces HCD provisions for apartments, condos, hotels, lodging houses and dwellings.

nodes.label: 1.8.4 Permits, Fees, Applications and Inspections
nodes.rationale: Written construction permits required prior to building work; references inspection sections in Division II.

nodes.label: 1.8.7 Alternate Materials, Designs, Tests, Methods
nodes.rationale: Permits use of alternate materials, designs, and methods of construction not specifically prescribed by this code.

nodes.label: Chapter 2 Definitions
nodes.rationale: Establishes specific meanings of technical terms used throughout the code.

nodes.label: R201 General
nodes.rationale: Scope and interpretation rules for definitions; refers to CBC for terms not defined here.

nodes.label: R202 Definitions
nodes.rationale: Master list of code-defined terms used in technical sections.

nodes.label: Accessory Dwelling Unit
nodes.rationale: An attached or detached residential dwelling unit that provides complete independent living facilities and is located on a lot with an existing primary residence.

nodes.label: Accessory Structure
nodes.rationale: A structure that is accessory to and incidental to that of the dwelling(s) and that is located on the same lot.

nodes.label: Addition
nodes.rationale: An extension or increase in floor area, number of stories, or height of a building or structure.

nodes.label: Alteration
nodes.rationale: Any construction, retrofit or renovation to an existing structure other than repair or addition that requires a permit.

nodes.label: Approved
nodes.rationale: Acceptable to the building official; HCD variant: meeting the approval of the enforcing agency.

nodes.label: Attic
nodes.rationale: The unfinished space between the ceiling assembly and the roof assembly.

nodes.label: Habitable Attic
nodes.rationale: A finished or unfinished habitable space within an attic.

nodes.label: Basement
nodes.rationale: A story that is not a story above grade plane.

nodes.label: Basic Wind Speed
nodes.rationale: Three-second gust speed at 33 feet above the ground in Exposure C as given in Figure R301.2(5)A.

nodes.label: Braced Wall Line
nodes.rationale: A straight line through the building plan that represents the location of the lateral resistance provided by the wall bracing.

nodes.label: Braced Wall Panel
nodes.rationale: A full-height section of wall constructed to resist in-plane shear loads through interaction of framing, sheathing, and anchors.

nodes.label: Building
nodes.rationale: Any one- or two-family dwelling or townhouse, or portion thereof, used or intended to be used for human habitation.

nodes.label: Building Official
nodes.rationale: The officer or other designated authority charged with the administration and enforcement of this code.

nodes.label: Carbon Monoxide Alarm
nodes.rationale: A single- or multiple-station alarm intended to detect carbon monoxide gas and alert occupants by a distinct audible signal.

nodes.label: Ceiling Height
nodes.rationale: The clear vertical distance from the finished floor to the finished ceiling.

nodes.label: Chimney
nodes.rationale: A primary vertical structure containing one or more flues, for carrying gaseous products of combustion to the outside atmosphere.

nodes.label: Cripple Wall
nodes.rationale: A framed wall extending from the top of the foundation to the underside of the floor framing of the first story above grade plane.

nodes.label: Dwelling
nodes.rationale: Any building that contains one or two dwelling units used or intended for living purposes.

nodes.label: Dwelling Unit
nodes.rationale: A single unit providing complete independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking and sanitation.

nodes.label: Emergency Escape and Rescue Opening
nodes.rationale: An operable exterior window, door or other similar device that provides for a means of escape and access for rescue in an emergency.

nodes.label: Grade Plane
nodes.rationale: A reference plane representing the average of the finished ground level adjoining the building at all exterior walls.

nodes.label: Guard or Guardrail
nodes.rationale: A building component located near the open sides of elevated walking surfaces that minimizes the possibility of a fall.

nodes.label: Habitable Space
nodes.rationale: A space in a building for living, sleeping, eating or cooking. Bathrooms, toilets, closets, halls, storage spaces are not habitable.

nodes.label: Building Height
nodes.rationale: The vertical distance from grade plane to the average height of the highest roof surface.

nodes.label: Lodging House
nodes.rationale: Any building containing not more than five guest rooms where rent is paid and that is occupied by the proprietor as their residence.

nodes.label: Live/Work Unit
nodes.rationale: A dwelling or sleeping unit in which a significant portion of the space includes a non-residential use operated by the tenant or owner.

nodes.label: Mezzanine
nodes.rationale: An intermediate level or levels between the floor and ceiling of any story.

nodes.label: Seismic Design Category
nodes.rationale: A classification assigned to a structure based on its occupancy category and the severity of the design earthquake ground motion at the site.

nodes.label: Shear Wall
nodes.rationale: Walls designed and constructed to resist racking from seismic and wind by use of masonry, concrete, cold-formed steel or wood framing per Chapter 6.

nodes.label: Sleeping Unit
nodes.rationale: A single unit that provides rooms or spaces for one or more persons including permanent provisions for sleeping.

nodes.label: Story
nodes.rationale: That portion of a building included between the upper surface of a floor and the upper surface of the floor or roof next above.

nodes.label: Story Above Grade Plane
nodes.rationale: Any story having its finished floor surface entirely above grade plane, or where the finished floor next above is more than 6 ft above grade plane.

nodes.label: Sunroom
nodes.rationale: A one-story structure attached to a dwelling with a glazing area in excess of 40 percent of the gross area of the structure's exterior walls and roof.

nodes.label: Townhouse
nodes.rationale: A building that contains three or more attached townhouse units.

nodes.label: Townhouse Unit
nodes.rationale: A single-family dwelling unit in a townhouse that extends from foundation to roof and that has a yard or public way on not less than two sides.

nodes.label: Multiple-Station Smoke Alarm
nodes.rationale: Two or more single-station alarm devices that are capable of interconnection so actuation of one causes all to operate.

nodes.label: Storm Shelter
nodes.rationale: A building constructed in accordance with ICC 500 and designated for use during a severe wind storm event such as a hurricane or tornado.

nodes.label: Lodging House (HCD 1)
nodes.rationale: HCD 1 California amendment definition of lodging house with not more than five guest rooms occupied by the proprietor.

nodes.label: Residential Care Facility (RF)
nodes.rationale: Any family home, group care facility or similar facility for 24-hour nonmedical care of persons in need of personal services or supervision.

nodes.label: Residential Care Facility for the Elderly
nodes.rationale: A facility chosen voluntarily by persons 60 years or over with varying levels of care, supervision, or personal care.
nodes.norm_label: residential care facility for the elderly

nodes.label: Limited-Density Owner-Built Rural Dwelling
nodes.rationale: Any structure consisting of habitable rooms occupied by one family with restricted use to designated rural areas.

nodes.label: Intermodal Shipping Container
nodes.rationale: A six-sided steel unit originally constructed as a general cargo container used for transport of goods and materials.

nodes.label: Chapter 3 Building Planning (a)
nodes.rationale: Building planning requirements: structural design, fire-resistant construction, light, ventilation, sanitation, egress.

nodes.label: R300 Site Drainage
nodes.rationale: Storm water drainage and grading per California Green Building Standards Code Chapter 4 Division 4.1.

nodes.label: R301 Design Criteria
nodes.rationale: Buildings shall be constructed to safely support all loads including dead, live, roof, flood, snow, wind, and seismic loads.

nodes.label: R301.1.1 Alternative Provisions
nodes.rationale: Permits AWC WFCM, AISI S230, ICC 400 as alternatives subject to limitations.

nodes.label: R301.1.3 Engineered Design
nodes.rationale: Where conventional construction contains elements exceeding R301 limits, engineered design per California Building Code applies.

nodes.label: R301.1.4 Intermodal Shipping Containers
nodes.rationale: Intermodal shipping containers repurposed for use as buildings shall be designed in accordance with Section 3115 of CBC.

nodes.label: R301.2 Climatic and Geographic Design Criteria
nodes.rationale: Buildings constructed per provisions limited by this section; criteria established by local jurisdiction in Table R301.2.
nodes.norm_label: r301.2 climatic and geographic design criteria

nodes.label: R301.2.1 Wind Design Criteria
nodes.rationale: Wind provisions using ultimate design wind speed in Table R301.2 from Figure R301.2(2).

nodes.label: R301.2.1.1 Wind Limitations
nodes.rationale: Wind provisions of code shall not apply where Vult equals or exceeds 140 mph in special wind region.

nodes.label: R301.2.1.2 Protection of Openings
nodes.rationale: Exterior glazing in buildings located in windborne debris regions shall be protected per ASTM E1886/E1996.

nodes.label: R301.2.2 Seismic Provisions
nodes.rationale: Buildings in seismic design categories shall comply with provisions of this section.

nodes.label: R301.2.4 Floodplain Construction
nodes.rationale: Buildings in flood hazard areas shall be designed to resist flood loads and damage.

nodes.label: R301.3 Story Height
nodes.rationale: Wind and seismic provisions limit story heights for various construction methods.

nodes.label: R301.4 Dead Load
nodes.rationale: Actual weights of materials and construction shall be used to determine dead loads.

nodes.label: R301.5 Live Load
nodes.rationale: Minimum uniformly distributed live loads for buildings.

nodes.label: R302 Fire-Resistant Construction
nodes.rationale: Construction, projections, openings, and penetrations of exterior walls; townhouse, two-family separation; foam plastics; flame spread.

nodes.label: R302.1 Exterior Walls
nodes.rationale: Construction, projections, openings, and penetrations of exterior walls relative to fire separation distance.

nodes.label: R302.2 Townhouses
nodes.rationale: Walls separating townhouse units shall be double walls or common walls per R302.2.1 or R302.2.2.

nodes.label: R302.3 Two-Family Dwellings
nodes.rationale: Dwelling units in two-family dwellings shall be separated by fire-resistance-rated wall and floor assemblies.

nodes.label: R302.5 Dwelling-Garage Opening Protection
nodes.rationale: Openings and penetrations between dwelling and private garage shall be protected.

nodes.label: R302.6 Dwelling-Garage Fire Separation
nodes.rationale: Fire separation requirements between dwelling unit and attached garage or carport.

nodes.label: R302.9 Flame Spread Index and Smoke-Developed Index
nodes.rationale: Wall and ceiling finishes flame spread and smoke-developed indices for interior walls and ceilings.
nodes.norm_label: r302.9 flame spread index and smoke-developed index

nodes.label: R302.11 Fireblocking
nodes.rationale: In combustible construction, fireblocking shall be installed to cut off concealed draft openings.

nodes.label: R302.13 Fire Protection of Floors
nodes.rationale: Floor assemblies that are not required by other provisions to be fire-resistance rated shall be provided with 1/2-inch gypsum or equivalent.

nodes.label: R303 Light, Ventilation and Heating
nodes.rationale: Habitable rooms shall have aggregate glazing area for natural light and openings for natural ventilation.

nodes.label: R303.1 Habitable Rooms
nodes.rationale: Habitable rooms shall have an aggregate glazing area of not less than 8 percent of floor area.

nodes.label: R303.3 Bathrooms
nodes.rationale: Bathrooms shall be provided with mechanical ventilation.

nodes.label: R304 Minimum Room Areas
nodes.rationale: Habitable rooms shall have a minimum floor area; minimum dimensions; height effect on room area.

nodes.label: R305 Ceiling Height
nodes.rationale: Habitable space, hallways, and bathrooms shall have a minimum ceiling height of 7 feet.

nodes.label: R306 Sanitation
nodes.rationale: Every dwelling unit shall be provided with toilet, kitchen, sewage disposal, and water supply.

nodes.label: R307 Toilet Fixture Spaces
nodes.rationale: Fixtures shall be spaced and bathtub/shower spaces lined with nonabsorbent surfaces.

nodes.label: R308 Glazing
nodes.rationale: Identification, hazardous locations, and skylights/sloped glazing requirements.

nodes.label: R308.4 Hazardous Locations
nodes.rationale: Specifies hazardous glazing locations including doors, windows, guards, wet surfaces, stairs.

nodes.label: R309 Garages and Carports
nodes.rationale: Garage floor surfaces, carport openness, flood hazard, automatic openers, and EV charging infrastructure.

nodes.label: R309.8 Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: California amendment requiring EV charging infrastructure in garages.

nodes.label: R310 Emergency Escape and Rescue Openings
nodes.rationale: Basements, habitable attics, and every sleeping room shall have an emergency escape and rescue opening.
nodes.norm_label: r310 emergency escape and rescue openings

nodes.label: R310.2 Emergency Escape and Rescue Openings
nodes.rationale: Minimum size, dimensions, and height from floor for emergency escape and rescue openings.
nodes.norm_label: r310.2 emergency escape and rescue openings

nodes.label: R310.4 Area Wells
nodes.rationale: Area wells, ladders/steps, drainage, and bars/grilles/covers/screens for below-grade EERO.

nodes.label: R311 Means of Egress
nodes.rationale: Dwellings shall be provided with a means of egress including egress door, hallways, stairways, and ramps.

nodes.label: R311.2 Egress Door
nodes.rationale: Not less than one egress door shall be provided for each dwelling unit.

nodes.label: R311.7 Stairways
nodes.rationale: Stairway width, headroom, vertical rise, treads/risers, landings, handrails, and special stairways.

nodes.label: R311.7.8 Handrails
nodes.rationale: Handrails shall be provided on at least one side of stairways with four or more risers.

nodes.label: R311.8 Ramps
nodes.rationale: Maximum slope, landings, and handrails for ramps.

nodes.label: R312 Guards and Window Fall Protection
nodes.rationale: Guards required at open-sided walking surfaces; window fall protection in dwelling units.
nodes.norm_label: r312 guards and window fall protection

nodes.label: R313 Automatic Fire Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: Automatic fire sprinkler systems for townhouses and one- and two-family dwellings.

nodes.label: R313.1 Townhouse Automatic Fire Sprinkler Systems
nodes.rationale: An automatic residential fire sprinkler system shall be installed in townhouses.
nodes.norm_label: r313.1 townhouse automatic fire sprinkler systems

nodes.label: R313.2 One- and Two-Family Dwellings Automatic Sprinklers
nodes.rationale: An automatic residential fire sprinkler system shall be installed in one- and two-family dwellings.
nodes.norm_label: r313.2 one- and two-family dwellings automatic sprinklers
